options.text: Writing a more detailed system prompt
Continuing to train an existing model on your own examples so its internal weights change
Adding a retrieval index to a model
Manually editing the model's answers after the fact

questions.explanation: Fine-tuning changes the model itself. Prompting and RAG change only what goes into the context. That's why fine-tuning is powerful for behavior and style but expensive and slow to iterate.

questions.prompt: Your company's product catalog changes weekly and you want the AI to answer questions about it. Best approach?

options.text: Fine-tune the model on the catalog every week
RAG — index the catalog and retrieve relevant entries per question
Hope the base model learned your catalog during training
Paste the full catalog into every prompt

questions.explanation: Changing facts belong in a retrieval index you can update instantly. Fine-tuning bakes knowledge into weights — stale within a week and costly to redo. Full-catalog pasting blows the context budget.

questions.prompt: A teammate's first idea for fixing an AI feature's inconsistent tone is 'let's fine-tune.' What's the better first step?

options.text: Agree — fine-tuning is always the strongest fix
Climb the ladder: improve the system prompt and add few-shot examples of the desired tone first; they're 10-100x cheaper to try
Add a RAG index of tone guidelines

questions.explanation: Prompt → few-shot → RAG → fine-tune, in that order. Tone is often fixable with a clear system prompt plus 2-3 examples — the same techniques you practiced in modules 02-04.

questions.prompt: When is fine-tuning genuinely the right call? (select all that apply)

options.text: Enforcing a strict output format across millions of calls where every prompt token counts
Teaching the model this week's product prices
Distilling a consistent brand voice that prompting can't reliably hold
Replacing a large prompted model with a smaller, cheaper specialized one

questions.explanation: Fine-tuning shines for behavior, style, and efficiency at scale. Fresh facts (b) belong in RAG — weights are the wrong place for anything that changes.
